essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: The Origin: Visa's canonical formulation of 'Do 100 Things' as a transformative practice for skill acquisition
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
1. Do it 100 times.

Write 100 songs, cook 100 omelettes, talk to 100 people. It never seems like a huge deal until you try it yourself. It’s manageable, and yet it stretches you, and you’ll be observably different at the end of it. Effective way to get a foothold on a new thing

essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
Here’s the magic of Do 100 Thing: the first 20 might look like crap, and you might think you’ll never get better if you do 1000, and then number 30 turns out better than you thought possible (h/t @shrinetothevine) https://t.co/Kz8cISI5Yk
Images:
- [Image #0] The image is a screenshot of a Twitter conversation between two users, @shrinetothevine and @visakanv. To recreate this image, follow these steps:

1. Set the background to a dark blue color.
2. Create a vertical thread of three tweets.
- The first tweet is from @shrinetothevine, featuring a cartoon profile picture of a person with purple hair and flowers. The text reads: "man at the rate i'm going i would have made 1000 cups of flat whites and i still wouldn't have figured out how to draw latte art" with 4 comments, 1 retweet, and 13 likes.
- The second tweet is from @visakanv, with a profile picture featuring a cartoon character with a crown. The text reads: "visa is stretching (hips) 🤸‍♂️ how many have you actually made? Do you take pics?" with 1 comment, 2 likes, and an upward arrow indicating a retweet.
- The third tweet is a reply from @shrinetothevine to @visakanv, using the same profile picture as the first tweet. The text reads: "No pics yet since 19/20 times have been just a brown gloop. Will probably start taking pics once I start getting vague shapes".
3. At the bottom of the image, include the timestamp "3:55 PM • 4/10/21" and the text "Twitter Web App" in blue.

By following these steps, you can recreate the Twitter conversation shown in the image.
